name: ramus
description: Ramus gives coding agents a disposable cloud Android emulator: run an APK, demo app or GitHub pull request build, then snapshot the screen, tap, type, read logs and share a live link. Requires a Ramus account or a free CLI trial.

interface.longDescription:
Ramus gives you a real Android device in the cloud. Ask it to start an emulator with the Ramus demo app, an APK already uploaded to Ramus, or the build from a GitHub pull request, then read the screen, tap, type, swipe, press keys, take screenshots and read device logs. Every session comes with a live link you can open in a browser to watch or take over the device, or to share with a teammate.

It is built for developers, QA and reviewers who want to see how an Android app behaves without installing an emulator.

Good to know:
- You need a Ramus account. You sign in with GitHub when you connect Ramus.
- Devices are disposable. Each session starts fresh and is discarded when it ends or after 30 minutes idle.
- Pull request previews need the Ramus GitHub App on the repository.
- Uploading a new APK from your computer, adb and hot reload need the Ramus CLI (in Codex or a terminal).
- Android only. Emulators run x86_64 system images without Google Play.
defaultPrompt: Start an Android emulator with the Ramus demo app and show me a screenshot.
Open the Ramus demo app on Android, tap through its first screens and tell me what you see.
Start an Android emulator and give me a link to watch it live in my browser.
